# COURTSIDE

**Who gets paid in the seconds after a tennis point, and what it takes to be first.**
Ojasva Mishra · Yoan Exposito · Rafael Penhas · Ian Hoang · University of Florida.
Gator Quant Hacks 2026 · Systematic Trading track · Paper: [`docs/NOTE.pdf`](docs/NOTE.pdf)
("COURTSIDE: Calling the Point Before It Lands. Predictive Ball Tracking and the Value of Speed in In-Play Tennis Markets").

Every tennis point moves a prediction market. On every resolved Polymarket ATP/WTA singles moneyline
from Oct 8, 2025 to Oct 3, 2026 (13,084 matches, $2.84B traded) we measured who makes and who
loses money in the seconds after each point. Then we priced the speed a computer-vision (CV) trader would need to
join the winners. The answer: speed is the edge, and the break-even feed delay is the result.

## Results

Same numbers and labels as the paper (location in brackets). IS = in sample; OOS = the held-out last
2,617 matches from 2026-08-25 14:15 UTC, opened once, blind, for v1 and **burned (non-blind)** for v2 and the CV
simulation, which were designed after it. ¢ = net cents per share after each match's own fee.

| | Result |
|---|---|
| **The edge** (fast tier: wallets trading ≤ 3 s after a score move, chosen walk-forward on past months) | +0.93¢ / +0.67¢ a share after fees (IS / OOS prints only; +0.75¢ if August's IS prints are included), positive in **9/9 IS and 3/3 OOS months** (11 of 11 calendar months, as in the video). Other takers lose (−0.89¢ / −1.43¢); copying the same trades 3 s later loses (−1.05¢ / −1.59¢). Chasing the move after a point (H1) loses −1.61¢ / −2.08¢. [Fig. 2a] |
| **v2** (frozen book at the fast tier's own fills; sizing `G_50pct_net100`, 100-share net cap, hold to resolution) | IS: Sharpe **14.5** [11.9, 17.4], +1.38¢ [1.17, 1.59], deflated Sharpe 0.997, max DD −2.0%, 7/7 months. **Burned OOS:** Sharpe **6.7** [1.9, 12.3], +0.60¢ [0.09, 1.13], deflated Sharpe 0.075 (at 3,386 trials); turnover 93 / 129× capital a year; +0.10¢ at ½ tick worse entry; **negative with costs doubled** (fees ×2 −0.34¢, all costs ×2 −0.84¢). PSR, MinTRL and a haircut over all 4,219 variants: 6 of 6 tests pass IS, 3 of 6 OOS (haircut Sharpe 0). A copier filled after the venue hold and the 1.98 s block lag loses (−0.47¢ IS, −1.37¢ OOS). The opportunity at their speed, not our execution. [Table 1, Fig. 2b] |
| **A firm with a licensed 0.5 s feed** (counterfactual: real prices, fills and fees, simulated calls, no feed bought) | Burned OOS +$15 / +$81 a day (pre-registered / post hoc). **Fresh holdout**, pre-registered at `dc95717` before its data were fetched (16 newer matches, 2 UTC days): −$20.5 / +$50.8 a day, CIs [−$96, +$57] and [−$38, +$141]: anecdotal. Break-even feed price a month: $384 / $2,397 on the burned OOS vs quotes of $1,250–$10,000. [Fig. 3] |
| v1 (copy the fast tier, $ sizing) | +1.16¢ IS; **−$36,056** on the held-out window (opened once, blind). [Table A1] |
| v2-safe (net cap 50, fixed after v2's OOS losses) | Sharpe 15.7 / 9.3 (IS / burned OOS); failed its blind unseen-market test (+1.21¢ [−0.02, 2.43]). [Table A1] |
| Blind and ex-ante tests | v2 on 11,307 never-examined markets: +2.02¢ in the IS period, +1.22¢ [−0.19, 2.65] in the OOS period (**FAIL**); maker v1 (FAILURE, −$379); the CV v3 rule (FAIL, −0.52¢). Every blind or ex-ante test of a tradable book failed. (The video's "blind tests: 2 pass · 4 fail" also counts two blind tests that are not tradable books: the table-tennis H3 call precision and v2 on unseen markets in the IS period.) [Table A1] |
| **Blind forward test** | pre-registered but not run within the hackathon window (HYPOTHESIS_V2.md A5). [Table A1, Appendix D] |
| **Speed requirement** (pre-registered, stamp lag 2.0 s) | Break-even feed delay **1.0–1.1 s** (1.09 s IS, 1.01 s OOS; +$4/day OOS at 1 s): the call must reach the venue **0.89 s before the umpire's stamp**. [Table 1, Eq. 1] |
| Measured latency | The book reprices 1.2 s *before* the official point stamp (n = 482); ESPN, Polymarket's sports feed and the WTA API trail the book by 28.2, 30.0 and 44.1 s. [Fig. A5a] |
| **Pipeline** (paper; order built, not sent) | Frame to unsigned order **54 ms** p50 (24 traces, own footage over WebRTC into the CV engine on a laptop). With a simulated 1 s feed, 65 ms network and the venue's 1 s hold the order is executable at **2,119 ms**, under the organisers' 3,000 ms bar. [Fig. A1] |
| CV, table tennis (real held-out footage) | The **live causal engine** called 4 of 41 misses before contact, none wrong (95% lower bound 51%), median lead 162 ms; the video's cold open shows a live-engine MISS call 325 ms before the ball passes the end line. L4 GPU: 119.9 fps, 0 of 102,120 frames dropped; **4.6 ms p50 per frame** to call-ready (the video's "6.9 ms on an NVIDIA L4" is the p50 per *emitted call*, a different statistic of the same run). The offline evaluation's 11 of 11 at 50 ms used a look-ahead feature. [Table A1, Fig. A5b] |
| CV, tennis (simulated physics) | A spin-aware tracker cuts landing error from 5.76 to 0.57 cm at 200 ms before the bounce, in simulation. Our tennis calls are simulated; the video's real rally (licensed stock footage) shows only the tracked ball trail (public detector, our linking). No tennis match video was used for trading. [Table A1] |
| **Capacity** | v2's OOS CI excludes zero only up to 1× size ($22,754 of capital); 5× loses. The CV book has no capacity at the pre-registered lag (Sharpe 2.7 / 0.8 at its smallest size); post hoc its Sharpe halves at $40,000 (OOS) and $73,000 (IS) of capital. It trades 0.22% of in-play volume but 9% of the fast tier's 0–3 s volume. [§7, Fig. A6] |
| Costs | Fees paid: 120 / 179 bps of notional for v2 (IS / OOS), 163–226 bps for the CV trader; with fees doubled every OOS CV cell loses (best −$13 a day). Price impact (log in size, fitted on 4.5 million IS orders) cuts v2's 1× OOS from $92 to $88 a day. v2 OOS after central fixed costs: −$75/day. At 1 s the CV book can pay at most $1,644 a month for data post hoc and $55 pre-registered, against quotes of $1,250–$10,000. COURTSIDE prices speed; it is not yet a business. [§7, Fig. A7] |
| Rigour | **4,219 variants in all; 3,410 strategy variants (the video's count); 3,386 in the deflated Sharpe** (the first adds the sensitivities and grids; the second adds the v2-safe grid to the third). 111 logged reads of held-out data, each classified; PBO 15% and deflated Sharpe 0.075 OOS: luck not ruled out out of sample; factor-neutral α t = 8.48 (max factor \|t\| 1.36). [Table A1, Appendices A and D] |

**The CV strategy at three assumed feed latencies** (simulated; assumed feed latency (licensed feed not purchased); parameters measured). Net $ a day, Sharpe and ¢ a share
[95% CI]; 20 seeds a cell. The trade set is the historical points the market later repriced by ≥ 4¢,
selected on outcomes (not ex ante), so every cell is an upper bound. [Table 1, Fig. A2]

| Feed latency (assumed) | **Pre-registered** (stamp lag 2.0 s), IS | **Pre-registered**, OOS | Post hoc estimate (3.14 s), IS | Post hoc estimate, OOS |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.5 s, best case | +$28, 4.0, +0.61¢ [0.08, 1.14] | +$15, 2.1, −0.02¢ [−1.22, 1.09] | +$133, 15.5, +1.21¢ [1.00, 1.42] | +$81, 12.2, +0.82¢ [0.39, 1.25] |
| **1 s, base case** | +$15, 2.1, +0.40¢ [−0.32, 1.08] | **+$4**, 0.3, −0.38¢ [−2.08, 1.21] | +$94, 11.9, +1.11¢ [0.85, 1.38] | +$57, 8.8, +0.66¢ [0.10, 1.19] |
| 3 s, the organisers' bar | −$13, −2.6, −1.35¢ [−3.15, 0.37] | −$13, −2.6, −1.69¢ [−4.85, 1.32] | −$6, −1.4, −0.79¢ [−2.26, 0.60] | −$11, −2.4, −1.47¢ [−4.45, 1.34] |
| Break-even feed delay | 1.09 s | 1.01 s | 2.23 s | 2.14 s |

Read the pre-registered columns first: at the 1 s base case the CV trader breaks even out of sample. The post hoc
stamp lag (3.14 s, 95% CI 2.23–3.22 s) assumes the fast tier are courtside humans; at its interval's
low end the OOS cell is only +$8/day. At 1 s the same clocks read point by point lose
(−$17/day); with no early CV calls the pre-registered OOS cell is −$13/day; and a replay on
9 matches' real recorded books, calling every point ex ante, loses in 36 of 36
delay × lag settings (−0.94¢ [−1.28, −0.58] at 1 s). We claim a price on each second of speed, not a bankable
CV P&L. The video's profit scene shows the 1 s post hoc estimate (94 and 57 dollars a
day, IS and OOS) with its label, and the pre-registered numbers on its stats rail.

## Reproduce

```bash
bash run.sh all          # = the four lines below; ~1.5-2.5 h, no keys
bash run.sh setup        # .venv + requirements.txt (Python 3.12+)                      ~1 min
bash run.sh data         # public Polymarket APIs, no keys; resumable, cached in data/   ~1-2 h
bash run.sh reproduce    # bash reproduce.sh: results/, every figure, docs/NOTE.pdf, these docs   ~15-20 min
bash run.sh docs         # README.md, docs/DEVPOST.md, docs/COMPLIANCE.md from results/paper/numbers.json  ~1 s
```

`reproduce.sh` runs, in order:

| Step | Produces |
|---|---|
| `run_all.py --oos` | H1–H6, calibration, tiers, walk-forward fast tier, v1 → `results/summary.json` |
| `scripts/v2_causal.py` | v2 on IS and the burned OOS, with ½- and 1-tick slippage → `results/v2/causal.json` |
| `scripts/v2_cost_stress.py` | v2 with fees doubled and all costs doubled → `results/v2/cost_stress.json` |
| `scripts/note_metrics.py` | annualised return and volatility, turnover, skew, worst month, bps, holdout share, data gaps → `results/v2/note_metrics.json` |
| `scripts/v2_figures.py`, `scripts/factor_regression.py`, `scripts/leverage_stats.py` | v2 figures, the factor regression, Markov leverage |
| `scripts/paper_figures.py`, `scripts/build_paper.py` | every paper figure (`results/paper/v2/`), `results/paper/numbers.json` (each number with its source), the LaTeX paper `docs/NOTE.pdf` via tectonic (needs `jinja2`, in `requirements.txt`); fails on > 5 main pages, < 11 pt text or the honesty grep; keeps the committed PDF if tectonic is missing |
| `scripts/build_docs.py` | this README, `docs/DEVPOST.md`, `docs/COMPLIANCE.md`, and the paper's label map `results/paper/labels.json` |

Things to know before running it:
- **Peek log.** On a fresh clone the first step builds the locked out-of-sample prints and appends one line to
  `results/oos_peeks.log`. That line records your run. Re-running on the same checkout appends nothing.
- **Frozen universe.** Polymarket's public event list keeps growing (a crawl late on 2026-10-03 also returns matches
  that started that day after ours: 13,109 instead of 13,084). `bash run.sh data` and `bash run.sh reproduce`
  run `scripts/freeze_universe.py`, which pins the cached event list to the 13,084 condition ids in
  `results/universe_conds.txt.gz`, so the 80/20 split is the paper's (the pinned code in `src/` is unchanged).
- **Not regenerated by `reproduce.sh`** (outputs are committed): the rigor pack (`scripts/rigor_pack.py`, ~25 s), the
  latency sweep and capacity study (`scripts/tier0_latency_sweep.py`, `scripts/capacity_study.py`), the six v2 lenses
  and their verifiers (`research/v2/<lens>/`), the blind out-of-universe tests (`scripts/expand_test.py`,
  `scripts/lowloss_test.py`), the end-to-end pipeline run (`scripts/e2e_proof.sh`) and ball tracking on HiPerGator.
- **Live recordings cannot be re-downloaded.** The order-book and score-feed recordings of 2026-10-03 behind the
  latency, depth and replay numbers were made with `src/live_recorder.py` and live in `data/live*` (gitignored); the
  derived numbers are committed in `results/` and `research/v2/{latency,livefill,blocklag}/`.
- **The blind forward test was not run** (`HYPOTHESIS_V2.md` A5: pre-registered, not run within the hackathon window;
  `results/forward_peeks.log` has no START line). `scripts/forward_test.py` is a one-shot that logs every run; if
  `results/v2/forward.json` ever exists, `bash run.sh reproduce` fills the one slot in the paper, this README and the
  Devpost text from it.

## Other commands

| Command | What |

| `bash run.sh setup --full` | also installs `requirements-extra.txt`: tracking (torch, OpenCV, ONNX Runtime) and the deck |
| `bash run.sh engine` | the paper-only COURTSIDE engine: order books on the committed sample, then 60 s of live public books |

| `bash run.sh live` | the paper trader on live public books, read-only (a tool; the pre-registered live session was stopped and is not used) |
| `python scripts/forward_test.py --start <UTC> --end <UTC>` | the frozen v2 rule on any window (the pre-registered forward test was not run: `HYPOTHESIS_V2.md` A5) |
| `sbatch hpg/track_*.sbatch`, `sbatch hpg/tennis_*.sbatch` | table-tennis and tennis tracking on HiPerGator (`src/tracking/README.md`, `src/tennis_tracking/README.md`) |
| `research/v2/<lens>/` | six optimisation lenses, each with two adversarial verifier reports |

## Layout

| path | what |
|---|---|
| `src/polymarket.py`, `src/tape.py` | public API client; universe, locked 80/20 split by match count, side-of-book classification |
| `src/tiers.py`, `src/fasttier.py` | markouts by seconds since the score event; the walk-forward fast tier (H6) |
| `src/v2.py` | the frozen v2 rule, runnable on any period |
| `src/markov.py` | exact point-level tennis Markov model (fair value, leverage) |
| `src/paper.py` | replays recorded live books; orders wait the venue delay plus latency, then walk the book |
| `engine/` | paper-only engine: v2 risk limits, $1,000 daily stop, kill switches (`engine/risk/limits.py`) |
| `src/tracking/`, `src/tennis_tracking/`, `engine/vision/` | ball tracking and the causal call engine |
| `results/` | every reported number; `results/paper/numbers.json` maps each paper number to its source |
| `docs/paper/` | the LaTeX source of `docs/NOTE.pdf` |
| `docs/templates/` | the templates of this README, the Devpost text and the compliance checklist |

## Data, sources and licences

- **Market data:** Polymarket Gamma, Data and CLOB APIs and its sports websocket; the Kalshi public market-data API.
  Public, no keys. Score feeds for the latency study: ESPN's public scoreboard and the WTA public API, read live;
  only derived timings are committed.
- **Factors:** Kenneth R. French Data Library (Fama–French market, size, value; momentum).
- **Video:** OpenTTGames (OSAI, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0); the table-tennis clips are derived from it under the same licence.
  The real tennis rally in the video is “Tennis Players Playing Match” by Gelato Prod, Pexels (Pexels License); source, licence terms and hashes in
  `results/viz/v60_assets/tennis_real/LICENSE.md`. Narration and music bed: AI-generated with ElevenLabs. The TrackNet
  tennis dataset (Huang et al. 2019) is used for evaluation only; no broadcast frames are included.
- **Pre-existing components** (not built during the event; disclosed per the Terms §14.2): BlurBall pretrained
  weights and code (MIT) on WASB-SBDT (MIT), used zero-shot for table-tennis ball detection; TrackNet weights and
  TennisProject / TennisCourtDetector code (no licence file; used unmodified for evaluation, not vendored or
  redistributed); in the video, a licensed stock tennis clip, “Tennis Players Playing Match” by Gelato Prod, Pexels (Pexels License), and an AI voice and music bed
  from ElevenLabs. Everything else was written during the event, with AI coding assistants.
- No API keys or licensed raw data are committed; raw data lives in `data/` (gitignored). The code only reads public
  data and never places an order.
